newsitem.title: DENMARK: Den Danske says no Norwegian buyout plans.
newsitem.headline: Den Danske says no Norwegian buyout plans.

text.p: Den Danske Bank said on Tuesday that it had no immediate plans to buy a Norwegian bank but would not rule out an acquisition if a suitable opportunity were to arise.
"We have no plans to buy a Norwegian bank, but on the other hand we do not deny that if an opportunity suddenly presents itself it could be considered," director Knud Soerensen told Reuters.
The bank is increasing its presence in Norway and on May 26 is to upgrade its representative office in Oslo to a full-scale branch.
Last month Den Danske, Denmark's biggest bank, took over Sweden's Ostgota Enskilda Bank after saying it had no purchase plans.

Norway's overbanked financial sector has seen fresh attempts at consolidation of late, with a group of 16 savings banks bidding for fourth largest bank, Fokus Bank and Fokus itself seeking to acquire niche mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank).
